proposal: The government proposes a 0.3% transaction fee on person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, paid by the customer, to fund cyber-fraud protection and keep UPI infrastructure free for small payments.

query: Indian government 0.3% UPI transaction fee above Rs 2000 fraud funding
bullets: Government weighs 0.3%-0.5% MDR on P2M UPI payments above ₹2,000 for merchants with >₹15m turnover.
Transactions above ₹2,000 make up ~4% of volume but ~67% of total UPI value, per Jefferies/Bernstein reports.
Proposed fee aims to fund cyber-fraud protection and sustain UPI infrastructure; small payments stay free.
Industry estimates suggest MDR revival could generate ₹50bn–₹100bn annually for payments firms like Paytm and Pine Labs.
Person-to-person UPI and small merchant transactions expected to remain exempt from any new charges.

headline: The fee will be rejected — rural and low-income India will force a political reversal despite urban middle-class tolerance.
say_do_gap: People say they oppose it (55% oppose, only 20% support) but 40% nationally still intend to adopt — yet rural adoption is just 31% versus 58% urban, so the policy survives in cities but collapses in the countryside.
summary: Opposition hardens across three rounds as the 0.3% fee on >₹2,000 P2M UPI payments is framed as a regressive tax on the poor. surprise: Adoption intent (40%) is double explicit support (20%) — agents complain but still plan to use UPI, revealing a silent-compliance trap that masks rural revolt risk.
fix: Shift the 0.3% fee from the customer to the merchant for all merchants under ₹50 crore annual turnover, and exempt person-to-merchant payments by users with verified annual income below ₹3 lakh.
rewrite: The government proposes a 0.3% merchant discount rate on person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000, borne by the merchant (not the customer), applicable only to merchants with annual turnover above ₹50 crore. Persons with verified annual income below ₹3 lakh are exempt from any fee on their outgoing P2M payments. Revenue funds cyber-fraud protection and keeps UPI infrastructure free for small payments and low-income users.
